questions.question: Which of the following correctly explains 'this' keyword in arrow functions?
options: Arrow functions have their own this binding
Arrow functions inherit this from the enclosing lexical scope
Arrow functions always refer to the global object
this inside arrow functions is determined at call time
questions.explanation: Unlike regular functions, arrow functions do not have their own 'this'. They capture 'this' from the lexical scope where they are defined.

questions.question: What will be logged?
options: undefined
ReferenceError
questions.explanation: Due to Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ), accessing 'let x' before its declaration in the function throws ReferenceError.

questions.question: Which array method does NOT mutate the original array?
options: splice()
push()
sort()
map()
questions.explanation: map(), filter(), slice(), concat() etc. return new arrays. splice(), push(), pop(), sort() (in place) mutate the original.

questions.question: What is event bubbling?
options: Events propagate from parent to child elements
Events propagate from child to parent elements
Events only trigger on the exact target element
Events are captured before reaching the target
questions.explanation: Bubbling is the default behavior where an event triggers on the target and then bubbles up through its ancestors.

questions.question: Which statement about closures is true?
options: Closures only work with global variables
A closure has access to variables from its outer function even after it returns
Every function creates a new closure automatically
Closures negatively impact performance and should be avoided
questions.explanation: A closure is created when a function remembers the variables from its lexical scope even after the outer function has finished executing.

questions.question: What does Promise.all() do if one promise rejects?
options: Waits for all promises to settle
Immediately rejects with the first rejection
Continues executing remaining promises
Returns undefined
questions.explanation: Promise.all() rejects as soon as any of the input promises rejects, and returns that rejection reason.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to deep clone an object (simple case)?
options: Object.assign({}, obj)
JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj))
Object.create(obj)
questions.explanation: JSON.parse(JSON.stringify()) is a common (though imperfect) way to deep clone plain objects. Spread and Object.assign only do shallow copies.
